title: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II on His Wild Cliff Booth Role and a Remarkable Year
excerpt:
The actor reflects on a busy 2026 and working with David Fincher.
His Cliff Booth character draws on 1970s Black action cinema.
body_md:
Yahya Abdul-Mateen II has reflected on an unusually varied year of work, moving between superhero comedy, television action, historical drama and a flamboyant supporting part in David Fincher's The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. The actor says the roles have little in common, and that their differences are precisely what made the year rewarding.

Written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by Fincher, the stand-alone follow-up to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood moves the story into 1977. Brad Pitt reprises his Oscar-winning role as Cliff Booth. Abdul-Mateen plays Roderick “Hot Rod” Harrison, a former professional football player who has reinvented himself as a movie star. Much of the character's screen presence appears inside a fictional film within the larger movie.

Hot Rod is informed by the Blaxploitation movement of the 1970s, with its distinctive action stars, heightened performances and cultural iconography. Abdul-Mateen cited Jim Brown and martial artist Ron van Clief as reference points, while explaining that he wanted to build his own larger-than-life creation rather than imitate either man. The character's championship rings, clothes, swagger and carefully chosen accessories communicate his public image.

The actor also took an unusual approach to the screenplay: he read only the scenes involving his character so he could remain a fan of the wider story. He describes Fincher as a highly engaged collaborator who welcomes conversations about performance. Although Fincher is famous for demanding multiple takes, Abdul-Mateen says the director's enthusiasm and attention to detail mattered more than that reputation. Fincher even encouraged the actors to moderate some of the more theatrical flourishes to keep the fictional movie's emotional stakes credible.

Elsewhere in 2026, Abdul-Mateen received a lead-actor Emmy nomination for Wonder Man, which the report says was canceled after its first season. He also starred in Netflix's Man on Fire and the historical thriller By Any Means. He says the nomination was not bittersweet because he valued the chance to play Simon Williams and would gladly revisit the character if invited.

Looking ahead, Abdul-Mateen hopes to continue playing charismatic, restrained and morally complex men while moving between genres. For him, Cliff Booth offered a rare chance to celebrate a specific era of filmmaking and experiment with a performance style he does not often get to use. The film was scheduled for an IMAX theatrical opening on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
